title: A $k$-Dimensional Version of the Largest Intersection Problem
summary: Suppose we have $r$ linearly independent hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$ (or $\mathbb{A}^m$) defined over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, whose intersection is at most $k$-dimensional. What is the largest possible number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points in the intersection? We conjecture an exact formula for this problem in both the projective and affine settings, assuming $q\geq d+1$.
